evidence: a combines David J. V. Jones's Before Rebecca and Welsh protest histories with David S. Jones's Rationalizing Epidemics and Broken Hearts, confirmed by Harvard. LC n81087188 identifies David J. V. Jones (1941–1994); b's n79098505 identifies David C. Jones (born 1943), the Calgary educational historian. LC no2013072274 identifies James Graham Wilson (born 1980), author of The Triumph of Improvisation; n80004337 identifies political scientist James Quinn Wilson (1931–2012), author of Thinking about Crime and Bureaucracy. They are different people. a additionally contains microscope and agricultural-wage articles from 1702 and 1911, impossible for either modern author.

a combines Jeffrey Lewis's Janus Face of Brussels with Juan Lewis's Guardians of the Aqueducts, independently attributed by their universities. Its LC n87862095 instead identifies Congressman John Lewis (1940–2020). b's n80025576 identifies religious-studies scholar James Roger Lewis (1949–2022), author of the New Age and new-religion books. The authority records describe different people, and a mixes additional authors.

LC n78071343 identifies Joseph Smith (born 1945), Exeter historian of US diplomacy and author of Illusions of Conflict. LC n80060957 identifies Joseph Henry Smith (1913–1981), Columbia legal historian and author of Appeals to the Privy Council. The records and the diplomatic-history versus colonial-law works identify two people.

LC n79089389 identifies Charles E. Rosenberg (born 1936), author of The Cholera Years and The Care of Strangers. LC n80079715 identifies Charles G. Rosenberg, the nineteenth-century writer of Jenny Lind (1850). These are separate authority identities; b's books appeared approximately eighty-five years before a's birth.

a combines R. D. Williams's Sixth Book of the Aeneid with R. B. Williams's Fifty Years of Anticoccidial Vaccines for Poultry, whose author and animal-health affiliation PubMed confirms. These are different authors gathered under one initial. b's Arius, On Christian Theology and sermons belong to theologian Rowan Williams, not this combined classical/veterinary corpus.

Cambridge's publisher credits a's William Appleman Williams and the American Empire, Peace Ballot and Liberal Party articles to J. A. Thompson. Jesus College's faculty bibliography credits b's Ideology and Modern Culture, The Media and Modernity, Political Scandal and Merchants of Culture to sociologist John B. Thompson. The specific author attributions and publication records distinguish them.

a combines R. R. Palmer's Age of the Democratic Revolution and Tom Paine article with Robert C. Palmer's The Feudal Framework of English Law, explicitly attributed by Michigan Law Review. Thus a contains multiple authors. b's Roy Palmer bibliography concerns British folklore and soldiers' songs and does not represent either of those careers.
